name: JD
author: Joerg Dommermuth

provenance.note: APD599 ships the extension, a per-keyword command reference (name/parameters/function/result/syntax/example) and the assembler source. The source, SOURCES/|jd.s, is PowerPacked and had never been read; pp20Decrunch unpacks it to 122 KB of commented 68k with a routine number per keyword. Its header states 'This file is public domain' and 'By Joerg Dommermuth', and `ExtNb equ 22-1` fixes slot 22 from the author's own build rather than from fingerprinting. The fixture keeps jd.s as distributed and jd.s.unpacked derived from it.
provenance.redistribution: The SOURCE (|jd.s) states it is public domain, in the author's own words. That covers the source only; the shipped binary carries no such statement and its terms remain unverified. The AMOS PD Library on CD (Weird Science, 1994), archive.org item cdrom-amospdcd, states Weird Science claims no copyright over the material, that parts are shareware with fees due, and that users should make no assumption that anything on it is public domain. Kept as a fixture.

findings: The largest third-party extension found on the disc: 130 named keywords covering date/time, strings, disk and screen utilities. Source and manual both present, so this is source tier. The disc's Extension_numbers file states the JD set installs at interpreter-config numbers 20, 21 and 22, which the source confirms for JD itself (ExtNb equ 22-1). Ported in src/runtime/jd.ts, which serves jd-5.9 as well: 5.9 renumbered the token table wholesale but changed only five keywords, and dispatch is by name.
notes: Date and time, string handling, disk and screen utilities — the biggest of the JD set.
